title: AST Wildlife Investigation: Lower Kalskag [AK25129043]
summary: On January 31, 2026, Alaska Wildlife Troopers in Bethel received a report of a dead muskox outside of Lower Kalskag. The area in and around Lower Kalskag (Game Management Unit (GMU) 19) has no open season for muskox, and initial reports indicated the muskox had not been salvaged. Wildlife Troopers responded and investigated the scene. Troopers determined that the muskox was shot illegally, and no efforts were made to salvage any of the meat. Through the service of search warrants and interviews Troopers determined 42-year-old Lower Kalskag resident Joseph Kameroff killed the muskox. summary: On December 31, 2025, at 5:55 am, Alaska State Troopers received a report of a man who had been shot on Winch Road in Fairbanks. The man fled to a nearby residence after being shot by Theodore Samsa, age 42, of Fairbanks. Troopers arrived on scene and made contact with the victim, who stated Samsa had shot him. While on scene, troopers heard gunshots coming from the incident location. Samsa barricaded himself in the residence and refused commands to surrender. He shot several times inside the residence, as well as trying to shoot at troopers on scene. SWAT deployed less lethal munitions, and Samsa eventually surrendered and was taken into custody. The victim was taken to a local hospital and is expected to survive. Samsa was arrested for Attempted Murder I and Assault I.

title: AST Failure To Salvage Moose: Farewell GMU 19C [AK25091599]
summary: On 09/08/2025, McGrath AWT contacted two hunters with a dead 52" bull moose at the Farewell Strip. Investigation determined Jeffery Harris, age 42 of Anchorage, took the moose on the evening of September 5th. The moose was left in the field for approximately 14 hours before being field dressed. Temperatures throughout the region were warm and wet. The meat of the moose spoiled due to not being properly cared for in a timely manner. Investigation also determined Harris took the two front shoulders, and other chunks of meat, and discarded them in the brush due to their putrid smell and colors. Harris was issued a citation for failing to salvage all edible meat. The moose rack and rotten meat were seized as evidence. Arraignment was set for October 9, 2025, in the Aniak Court.
sourceAttribution: Source: Alaska State Troopers Daily Dispatch

summary: On July 11, 2025, at around 1:00 am, a fight occurred in a cell between two inmates at the Anchorage Correctional Center. Officers used force to put Foreman on the ground and began restraining him. While being restrained, Foreman kicked an officer and was placed in leg restraints. Shortly after he was restrained, Foreman became unresponsive, and lifesaving efforts were started immediately by correctional staff and later the Anchorage Fire Department. Despite these efforts, Foreman was declared deceased at the facility. His next of kin have been notified, and his body has been sent to the State Medical Examiner’s Office for autopsy.

title: AST Terroristic Threatening Second Degree: Soldotna [AK20015245]
summary: On 3/2/2020 at approximately 2100 hours, Soldotna AST responded to multiple disturbances in the Soldotna and Kenai areas. Subsequent investigation and with assistance of the Kenai Police Department, Andrew Malone, age 30 of Kenai, was taken in to custody on a single charge of Terroristic Threatening in the second degree. Malone was remanded to Wildwood Pretrial Facility where he was held without bail pending arraignment.

title: AST Assault 4th DV, Criminal Mischief 5th DV: Wasilla [AK20015251]
summary: On 3/3/20 at approximately 0001 hours Alaska State Troopers responded to a report of a disturbance at a residence off of Singing Woods Drive in Wasilla. Investigation revealed Summer Williams, age 27 of Wasilla assaulted a family member and damaged property valued under $250. Williams was arrested for Assault 4th DV and Criminal Mischief 5th DV. She was transported to MSPT where she was remanded with no bail.
